work.title: First public release of Readela 0.2.0 through the Chrome Web Store and Firefox Add-ons (AMO)
work.ownerAuthorization: Owner execution authorization of 2026-10-03, recorded in the managerial work unit ENT-198. It authorizes the bounded release workflow for the 0.2.0 build already on main: this release Preflight and its Gates; the focused repository changes needed for truthful store readiness; final verification, build and hash evidence; integration through the protected main; and submission of the exact Gate-approved Chrome and Firefox artifacts to the already-selected Chrome Web Store and Firefox AMO routes when authenticated provider access and every mandatory prerequisite exist. No routine approval stop is required for those steps. It does not permit creating an owner identity or developer account where identity verification is required, exposing or persisting credentials, bypassing multi-factor authentication, incurring a fee or payment, accepting a developer agreement or legal attestation on the owner's behalf, making a legal or trademark claim, renaming the product, or broadening scope. Work stops at exactly such a boundary after every safe prior step is complete.

providerRequirements.authority: Official Google (developer.chrome.com) and Mozilla (extensionworkshop.com) documentation read on the date above. Dashboard wording is confirmed on the live dashboards at submission time; this record does not freeze it.
chromeWebStore: Developer registration with a one-time fee and acceptance of the developer agreement and policies; publishing requires two-step verification on the account. Owner-only.
Store icon 128x128 PNG in the package (present: icons/icon-128.png); 1 to 5 screenshots at 1280x800 or 640x400; one 440x280 small promotional image; marquee image optional.

Privacy practices: a single-purpose statement, a justification for every permission and for site access, a remote-code declaration, user-data handling disclosures and the certifications, and a privacy-policy URL. Google states that handling must be disclosed even when data is processed or stored only locally, so Readela discloses its local handling of website content and does not claim that it handles no user data.
Submission enters review; an accepted item is not published until Google's review completes and the developer publishes within 30 days.
firefoxAmo: A Mozilla account connected to AMO. Owner-only where account creation, e-mail confirmation or multi-factor verification is required.

Extensions whose packaged code is generated by a bundler must submit readable source with a README that lets a reviewer rebuild the package; Mozilla's reviewer environment is Ubuntu 24.04 with Node 24.14.0 and npm 11.9.0, and deviations must be documented.

Since 2025-11-03 every new extension must declare browser_specific_settings.gecko.data_collection_permissions; required ["none"] states that nothing is collected or transmitted and matches the project contract.

Listing metadata: name, summary, description, up to two categories, license, support e-mail and site, reviewer notes; a privacy policy is mandatory only when data leaves the device, and Readela provides one anyway. Submission is validated automatically, then reviewed; signing follows approval.

risk.tierNote: Product rigor with the exact-artifact identity discipline the published-artifact boundary calls for: every submitted file is bound by SHA-256 to one frozen source commit, every Gate names the artifact it assessed, and a published store version cannot be withdrawn and reused, only superseded.
risk.targetedVerification: The trust-relevant changes are the public artifacts and the public declarations about them. They receive: the full existing test run on the release-readiness head; a clean-clone build reproduced twice with equal digests; a check that the submitted listing and privacy statements equal the manifest and the privacy document of the exact artifact; and read-back of the provider's recorded version, identifier and status after each submission.
